transcript: Elon Musk took rockets from SpaceX and put them inside a Tesla, and the crazy part is the car flipped upside down and flew. Hear me out. Tesla just took a car, drove it up a curved ramp until it was completely upside down, and then made it fly. And if you think this came out of nowhere, Elon called it way back in August. Someone complained that we got AI instead of flying cars, and Elon replied with just four words: You will get flying cars. Then the teaser showed the car upside down with a line from Back to the Future. So here's what actually happened. The car shot off the end of the ramp, flipped in the air, used air thrusters to turn itself straight, and landed safely. Then it jumped right over the whole Tesla lineup. And in a live run, it went from 0 to 60 in less than 1 second. Elon even said they needed a real crowd there just to prove it wasn't AI. But here's the part nobody is talking about. In 2017, Elon went on stage and made fun of flying cars. He said if cars were flying over your head, you'd be scared something would fall off and hit you. And that very same year, he showed off this exact Roadster. A few months later, he tweeted that SpaceX rockets might help it fly. The idea was so exciting that even Sam Altman paid $50,000 to book one. Then the car got delayed again and again for nine years. It got so bad that Sam Altman canceled his booking, asked for his money back. Now, the catch. Nobody was inside the car during the stunts because it was driving itself. The flights lasted only a few seconds, and the flying version is invite-only, isn't allowed on normal roads, and production only starts in 2028. But the same man who laughed at flying cars just posted this: Turns out the future does have flying cars. So tell me, would you actually buy one? And what do you think it will cost? Drop your guess in the comments. And I share stories like this the moment they drop in my free WhatsApp community. So go check it out, the link is in my bio.
